newsitem.title: INDIA: India IDBI accepts Booz Allen revamp plan.
newsitem.headline: India IDBI accepts Booz Allen revamp plan.

text.p: The board of Industrial Development Bank of India (IDBI) has decided to restructure itself on the lines suggested by consultancy firm Booz Allen & Hamilton, IDBI chairman S.H. Khan said on Monday.

Khan told reporters IDBI had appointed the consultancy to study its role and advise it on strategic repositioning to maintain its leadership in the context of new opportunities and challenges in the environment following liberalisation of financial services.
"The recommendations will be processed by a task force created for the purpose and will be taken up for implementation in a phased manner," an IDBI statement said.
All recommendations of Booz Allen, barring those which have regulatory and statutory implications, will be taken up, Khan told a news conference.

"IDBI's strategic objective should be to repositon itself as India's premier wholesale bank through a full range of wholesale products -- lending, capital markets, advisory and risk management -- through an integrated group structure," IDBI said.
Each of these would be a profit centre, Khan said.
While continuing its focus on the core business of project financing, Booz Allen has recommended lendings to include offering of working capital and short-term finance to its existing customer base.
For facilitating effectve treasury management, it should have greater access to money market instruments like certificates of deposit and fixed deposits, it said.

The consultants recommended that IDBI reassign its refinance business and resources to the Small Industries Development Bank (SIDBI) and then reduce or dispose of its holding in SIDBI and the Industrial Finance Corp of India.

IDBI owns about 28 percent of IFCI. Khan said the government was against IDBI selling its stake in IFCI. It would also not consider selling its holdings in SIDBI as it would mean amendment of the SIDBI Act, Khan said.
The following are the major recommendations on improving performance:

+ Reorganisation of head office into divisions oriented towards customers -- corporate and middle market, products (capital market and treasury and funding) and support service functions (research and planning, rehabilitation).
The head office should look after large corporate borrowers and reallocate the mid-corporate customers to branch offices.

+ The branches should be grouped into four categories depending on products and volume of business handled. The branches would be administratively controlled by four zonal offices. Zonal managers will be involved in target setting, performance monitoring and providing guidance, it said.

+ With a view to cutting down response time, Booz Allen has recommended greater decentralisation of operations to branches. It is proposed that corporate office will handle projects of size above 2.0 billion rupees, Grade A branches upto 2.0 billion rupees, Grade B branches upto 1.0 billion rupees and Grade C branches will focus exclusively on fund raising activities.

+ The consultants have proposed establishment of credit committee at the head office and the four zones. Besides screening proposals, these committees will exercise powers for sanction of credit and also review the asset quality in their respetitive zone operations.

Zonal committees will have the power to sanction upto 200 million rupees and the credit committee upto 500 million rupees. Assistance above 500 million will continue to be sanctioned by the executive committee.
The zonal committee will meet at respective zones fortnightly and credit committee at head office weekly.
